correctness.rationale: Deleting the forbidden u->v leaves one excess incoming edge at u and one excess outgoing edge at v. Every admissible tour adds an integral u-to-v unit flow; an optimal flow uses a shortest permitted path alone. All original edges lie on directed cycles, so deletion leaves the underlying graph connected and a balanced augmentation really does have an Euler tour. For end-position markers the all-zero vertex cannot be entered or cannot be left, respectively. For an interior marker, d=1 is forbidden. At 2<=d<n the spelled word is covered by its prescribed prefix and suffix; the two forced ones must lie outside the opposing block but inside the first and last forbidden-candidate windows. This forces d=i+1=j+1. In that case every window of the unique spelling contains both ones. Off center d=n leaves one free bit, and zero there makes the first window forbidden. One there prevents the first and last ones from creating a forbidden window and cannot itself be preceded by i and followed by j zeros. A shortest path is simple, so its factors are distinct and the set of extra traversals is unique; this is not uniqueness of the cyclic word. Complementation preserves all conclusions. Independent replay `cd /workspace && python3 review_replay.py 1` checked all 75 deletion cases of orders 3..12, including shortest-path counts and the prescribed spellings, plus literal existence at length 9 versus nonexistence at length 8 for 010. This supports, not replaces, the all-order argument. The frozen verification and code (including its Euler-witness checks) were inspected but not executed.

value.rationale: Deleting the unique sparse marker pattern is a motivated perturbation of universal cyclic coverage. Knowing whether coverage can coexist with avoidance, exactly how much repetition is forced, and exactly which factors must repeat gives a concrete construction and obstruction benchmark. Neither the odd-centered shortcut nor the uniqueness of the duplication pattern follows from being able to compute a shortest path in each example.
